Strict convexity/concavity and positive derivatives prove all multipliers and folds. Monotonic thresholds and endpoint expansions follow analytically by the implicit-function theorem. value.rationale: The source motivates fixed-point-free parameter design to avoid attracting nonchaotic basins. This theorem supplies an exact exhaustive test, not a numerical diagram, for all three cosine-map parameters, and an open four-fixed-point phase with two distinct attracting states. In contrast to the related fractional-power family, the four-fixed-point phase exists at every breakpoint. The monotone dual fold functions and sharp quadratic narrow-branch bounds quantify the robustness of parameter choices. The claim is a complete natural fixed-point classification, not a convenience slice; no cryptographic or global-chaos conclusions are inferred.
